page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Daldv6 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, with 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, which positions it as a compute-oriented resource with a lower memory-to-CPU density. It is equipped with 945 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests reveal a notable bottleneck: while cached small-block reads and large-block writes perform at average levels, uncached large-block read memory bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds for text generation using a small 135M model are strong, while prompt processing and medium 7B model inference remain average.

The D16alds_v6 offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require extensive memory footprints. The inclusion of 945 GB of local storage provides high resource density for local caching and temporary data storage. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 and the weak uncached large-block memory read bandwidth represent key tradeoffs, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory processing. Recommended workloads include single-threaded applications, text processing pipelines, lightweight web serving, and software compilation.
